questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in what position?
questions.correctAnswerText: Normal
questions.explanation: The air supply control should be set to "normal" position when pulling a trailer. This is the correct setting for tractor protection controls.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from escaping the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no semi-trailer attached. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, at what angle should the seals be pressed together?
questions.correctAnswerText: 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a serious leak.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
questions.explanation: The best way to spot a trailer skid is to use your mirrors. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure the trailer is in the correct position.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will often continue moving straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is more likely with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: If your trailer begins to skid, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes to let the wheels regain grip. Once the wheels have traction again, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: When braking a trailer with anti-lock brakes, how should you brake?

options.text: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: With anti-lock brakes, brake normally. Do not pump the brakes or use extra force. Brake as you normally would.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows wheels to lock up.
It prevents wheels from locking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking during hard braking. If ABS detects wheel lockup starting, it reduces braking pressure.

questions.question: Before driving, make sure air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for air escaping.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure the air brake system reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping from the rear shut-off valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: Before driving, you can check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Checking for moving air inside each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure the air brake system reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping from the rear shut-off valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, keep all shut-off valves open except the rear valves on the last trailer. This ensures air reaches the brakes on all trailers and prevents air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two air lines.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: If colors mark the glad hands, which color is used for service lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Service lines are usually blue. Emergency lines are usually red.

questions.question: When traveling below 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller ones.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over a trailer.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause trailers to tip over. The last trailer is most likely to tip. Know your vehicle's rearward amplification and drive carefully.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Does not change braking in any way.
Gives the driver more control when braking.
Puts extra strain on other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives the driver more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) on just the trailer or on one axle still gives the driver better control when braking.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity from the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semitrailer attached. Bobtails are harder to stop and need a longer distance to come to a complete stop than a loaded tractor and semitrailer.
